summary: A 1975 slight revision of RFC 686, on the subject of print files in FTP. It is part of a long discussion that includes RFC 640, RFC 630, RFC 542, RFC 454, RFC 448, RFC 414, RFC 385 and RFC 354.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC argues for making practical changes to the existing FTP-1 rather than waiting for FTP-2. It focuses on print-file handling, the SRVR command and how reply codes should work.

subtitle: Brian Harvey's proposals for addressing print files and reply-code differences in FTP-1.

tldr.problem: The author describes differences among FTP-1 implementations and argues that waiting for FTP-2 should not block practical fixes to FTP-1.
tldr.mechanism: He proposes recipient-side print-file formatting, SRVR parameters for recipient-specific details, a 200 reply after HELP, and changes to experimental and failure reply codes.
tldr.outcome: RFC 691 is a slight revision of RFC 686 and presents the author's proposals, including a request to adopt some changes if no one objects before June 1.

today: The unit metadata records RFC 691's status as Unknown. It revises RFC 686 and presents Brian Harvey's proposals during the FTP-1 and FTP-2 discussion.

sections.title: A Revision of an FTP Proposal
sections.content:
Brian Harvey says RFC 691 is a slight revision of RFC 686, mainly changing its discussion of print files. It also adjusts the reply-code list to reflect lists in RFCs 354, 454, 542 and 640.

Harvey suggests that, if there are no objections before June 1, participants treat several changes as official: HELP should return 200, SRVR should be used as described, and permanent 4xx errors should become 5xx. He says the suggestions are not necessarily the best possible changes, but are easily doable.
sections.plainLanguage: The author revises his earlier note, mostly on print files and reply codes. He asks readers to object before June 1 if they disagree with some suggested changes.

sections.title: Print Files and Recipient-Specific Details
sections.content:
For ASCII or EBCDIC print files, Harvey argues that the transmitted data should contain Fortran control characters and be sent as is. The recipient, rather than the server, should reformat it if necessary.

He proposes using the SRVR command for information that affects only the receiving system and not the bytes sent over the network. He gives SRVR T for a Telnet print file and SRVR N for normal operation, which turns off an earlier SRVR setting. He also argues that sender programs should be able to pass through these recipient-specific values without interpreting them.
sections.plainLanguage: Harvey says the receiving system should format print files for its own printer. He proposes SRVR for recipient-only settings that do not change the transferred data.

sections.title: Reply Codes and Proposed Changes
sections.content:
Harvey proposes that HELP end with reply code 200. He also argues that experimental reply codes should remain within 000 through 599 and use x9x or xx9 patterns, so user programs can interpret the first digit.

He supports distinguishing temporary and permanent failures using 4xx and 5xx replies, respectively. For STAT, he describes existing replies as one or more 151 information messages followed by 200 END OF STATUS, and proposes documenting behavior that he says was already in use.
sections.plainLanguage: The author wants reply codes to tell programs clearly whether a command succeeded, failed temporarily or failed permanently. He also proposes a consistent ending code for HELP.

sections.title: Why Fix FTP-1
sections.content:
Harvey argues against waiting for FTP-2 to solve the problems he identifies. He says many sites were using FTP-1 and transferring files, and that some proposed FTP-2 changes would require coordinated reprogramming. He favors changes that could be made within FTP-1 without requiring every host to switch at once.

The RFC ends with a list of existing FTP-1 reply codes and proposed replacements. The document records Harvey's argument and recommendations rather than reporting that all of them were adopted.
sections.plainLanguage: Harvey prefers smaller changes that existing FTP-1 users could make without waiting for a full protocol replacement. The list at the end shows his proposed reply-code changes.
